Paydaş: All the social parties with which the enterprise interacts, that are affected by the enterprise's activities, and that affect the enterprise through their activities.
Pazar ya da piyasa: The physical or virtual environment where buyers and sellers come together, and in this process the prices of products are determined.
Per Se: In competition law, per se rules have been adopted to deem unlawful, in almost all cases, those behaviors whose natural and inevitable effects are clearly anticompetitive and for which a detailed study is not needed to show that they are unlawful. These are the practical rules of the US judicial process. Per se rules are accepted in cases where experience shows that certain behaviors will cause serious anticompetitive outcomes and can hardly ever be justified. Accordingly,
Perfect Competition: A hypothetical market model in which, owing to the presence of a great many buyers and sellers, it is not possible for individuals to influence prices, so prices are taken as given; entries into and exits from the market are entirely free; there is the opportunity of full information about market conditions; goods are homogeneous; the rational behavior pattern directed toward profit maximization is dominant; and production and exchange can be carried out free of any limitation. It is known that such a market cannot exist in reality
Performans Göstergesi: The scales producing quantitative information about projects and enabling the project targets to be defined in a clear and measurable way.
Persons: The administrative fines of up to five percent of the fine imposed on the undertaking or undertaking association, given to the managers or employees of the undertaking or undertaking association whose determining influence in the infringement is established, regulated in Article 16(4) of the Competition Act in the event that fines relating to the substance are imposed on undertakings or undertaking associations.
Phillips eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between the unemployment and inflation rates, all else being constant.
Pigou etkisi: The analysis put forward by the British economist Arthur Cecil Pigou, stating that when the general price level decreases, aggregate demand will increase owing to the appreciation of wealth.
Pigou vergisi: The tax imposed on economic activities creating a negative externality.
Piyasa aksaklığı: The situation of the fall in social gain as a result of the market's effectiveness in production or distribution declining.
Piyasa arzı: Or in short S: the quantity of a product that all the sellers in the market want to sell, depending on different prices, in a given period.
Piyasa dengesi: The situation in which, in a given period, the quantity of a product demanded in the market equals the quantity supplied.
Piyasa dengesizliği: The short- or long-term situation in which the market cannot reach the equilibrium point for internal or external reasons.
Piyasa Faiz Oranı: The interest rate paid for deposits and other investments, determined in the money market according to the interaction of money supply and money demand.
Piyasa gücü: The measure describing to what extent a buyer or seller can influence the market price of a certain product.
Piyasa Katılımcıları Anketi: A survey applied monthly by the CBRT with the aim of obtaining the expectations of decision-makers and expert persons in the financial and real sectors regarding fundamental macroeconomic variables such as consumer inflation, the exchange rate, the current account balance, GDP growth rate and interest rates. To access the Market Participants Survey
Piyasa takas fiyatı: Or the clearing price: the price at which transactions take place when the market is in equilibrium.
Piyasa talebi: Or in short D: the quantity of a product that all the buyers in the market want to purchase, depending on different prices, in a given period.
Piyasa ya da pazar: The physical or virtual environment where buyers and sellers come together, and in this process the prices of products are determined.
Piyasa Yapıcılığı Sistemi: A system in which, with the aim of increasing effectiveness in primary market transactions and facilitating the functioning of secondary markets, the treasury or central banks accept as counterparty only the banks and certain other institutions it selects according to certain criteria, in transactions such as debt security issuance (auction) and foreign exchange intervention. The institutions selected under the name of market maker have obligations such as transacting uninterruptedly in the secondary markets, giving quotations, and purchasing a certain amount of an issue.
Piyasa yapısı: The concept describing the properties of the economic interaction arising as a result of the numerical and size distribution of the buyers and sellers in the market.
Piyasa yoğunlaşması: The conceptual measure describing how competitive a market is, by looking at the distribution of firms' market shares.
Piyasa ürün sepeti: Or the basket of goods: the list of products determined with the aim of representing the whole of the economy or a certain subsection of it.
Piyasaya giriş engeli: Or a barrier to entry: the natural or artificial restrictions that make it difficult to sell or buy in a certain market.
Planlı toplam harcama: Or in short AE: the market value of those among all the final goods and services produced using a country's resources in a given period whose purchase is desired.
Platform Economies: Platform economies are the formations enabling two (or more) different but interlinked user groups operating in a two (or multi)-sided market to interact in a way that creates value for at least one of the sides. Their most frequently observed examples are online demand-coordinating platforms (online marketplaces, general or specialized search sites) and hardware/software platforms.
Politika etkisizliği önermesi: The view maintaining that, under rational expectations, the state cannot create a permanent effect on production and employment by using monetary policy.
Politika karışımı: The state's using fiscal and monetary policies together in order to influence the macroeconomy.
Portföy: The asset basket formed from investments having different risk properties.
Portföy Yatırımları: Portfolio investments, which can be defined as investments made in securities, generally include the transactions made with non-residents using stocks, the debt instruments in the form of bills and bonds issued by public or private institutions, and other money market instruments.
Portföy Yönetim Şirketi: The capital market institutions established in the form of joint-stock companies whose main line of activity is the establishment and management of funds.
Position: The strengthening by an undertaking holding a dominant position in a market of its dominant position, particularly by increasing market share, at the end of a concentration transaction.
Potansiyel GSYH: The level of real GDP that is sustainable, depending on natural, demographic, technological or institutional constraints.
Potansiyel işgücü: Among the persons of working age who are neither employed nor unemployed: those who are seeking work but are not in a state to start work within a short time, and those who, without seeking work, have a desire to work and are in a state to be able to start work within a short time.
Potential Competitor: In the event of a small and permanent increase in prices, the undertaking having the possibility (and desire) of entering the market, bearing the necessary conversion costs or making the mandatory investments, is accepted as a potential rival.
Pozisyon Fazlası: Refers to the net surplus position held in foreign currency, securities or any financial instrument. For example, having a 10 million US dollar cash surplus position means having, net (after cash US dollar debts are deducted), 10 million US dollars in cash in a portfolio. In other words, it expresses a surplus holding in an instrument.
Pozitif dışsallık: The beneficial effect an economic activity has on persons who are not party to that activity.
Pozitif çözümleme: The analytical approach treating economic behavior and systems with an objective perspective, trying only to describe them without judging.
Pozitif çıktı açığı: Or an expansionary gap: the situation in which, in the short run, real GDP is above potential GDP, and hence the economy is considered to be in an expansion period.
Price Leadership: Refers to the situation in which an undertaking in a dominant position, or whose leadership is accepted by the others, changes its prices and the other undertakings in the market adopt and follow this price. Apart from the price leader's being in a dominant position, on what criteria it is determined/selected is a matter that varies from market to market and requires research. Nevertheless, when price leadership is adopted to facilitate tacit agreement, the price leader generally has a high
Price Recommendation: Suppliers' recommending the price at which a good will be resold is evaluated, within the scope of competition law, according to whether this recommendation turns into fixed or minimum price setting. The recommended price practice has two drawbacks from the standpoint of competition law.
Price Rigidity: Price rigidity refers to the price of a good, service or production factor remaining constant despite perceptible changes in supply and demand conditions, or changing in only one direction. Price rigidity, also called price stickiness, is a matter closely concerning competition policies. For price rigidity is a phenomenon that can stem from a lack of competition and negatively affect social welfare. Market structure and undertakings' behaviors can create price rigidity. In general
Primary Market: Special terms are used to refer to the markets where the sale of the main product and the side products that need to be purchased along with it or later than it is realized. The first product the customer buys is called the primary product, and the product needed later for that product to be usable the secondary product. The markets where the trade of the primary and secondary products takes place are, respectively, the primary/fore market and the secondary/aftermarket
Producer Surplus: The difference between the price the producer actually sells at and the price it is willing to sell at is called the producer surplus. The concept of producer surplus is dealt with within the scope of competition economics/policy because, when there is a price increase in the market, while the consumer surplus decreases, this decrease is not transferred as an equal amount of producer surplus (and the deadweight loss thereby formed) results in a fall in total social welfare.
Production Joint Ventures: The joint ventures formed with the aim of producing. Production joint ventures can be fully functional, or can also emerge as non-fully functional (partially functional) joint ventures undertaking only a limited part of the parent undertakings' fields of activity. The reason for partial functionality is generally that, because these ventures make use of the parent undertakings' raw material sources and technical knowledge, they cannot behave independently in the markets, and the sale of the produced products is left to the parent undertakings
Profit: In economic theory and in the accounting discipline it is possible to speak of two separate profit concepts that differ from one another. The profit concept used in accounting expresses the revenue surplus remaining in the firm's hands after it has covered the costs of all the inputs it used in production. Profit in the economic sense, on the other hand, expresses the revenue surplus formed after the opportunity cost of producing the good is also added to the total costs. In this case, a firm earning zero profit in the economic sense still earns normal
Profit Maximization: One of the fundamental assumptions on which microeconomic theory rests is that firms realize their production quantities at the level that maximizes their profits. At this production quantity, the price level forming in the market is named 'the price at the level where profit is maximized'. In microeconomic theory this point is the price formed according to the demand function at the production level where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.
Program: The programs applied in countries such as the United Kingdom and South Korea, expressing the giving of rewards to those who are not part of a cartel but somehow have knowledge of the cartel's existence and report it.
Programı: The support program implemented by the Ministry of Industry and Technology with the aim of raising Turkish industry's competitiveness, innovativeness and efficiency, taking a greater share of global exports, predominantly producing high-technology products, and transforming industry into a structure possessing qualified labor and at the same time sensitive to the environment and to society. Liquidity: the degree to which enterprises' assets can be quickly and easily converted into cash.
Proje Bazlı Teşvik Sistemi: (Super Incentive) The incentive system that entered into force with the Decree on the Granting of Project-Based State Aid to Investments No. 2016/9495, aiming at the project-based support of innovative, R&D-intensive and high value-added investments that will meet our country's critical needs arising at present or in the future, will ensure supply security, will reduce external dependence, and will realize its technological transformation.
